definitions.gloss: memory (ability); ability to learn and remember things
definitions.explanation: One's capacity to memorize and retain information. Often used with adjectives like good or bad to describe someone's memory skills.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{物覚|ものおぼ}えがいい。
{最近|さいきん}、{物覚|ものおぼ}えが{悪|わる}くなった。
examples.english: My memory has gotten worse lately.

examples.japanese: {物覚|ものおぼ}えが{早|はや}いので、{仕事|しごと}をすぐ{覚|おぼ}えた。
examples.english: I'm a quick learner, so I picked up the job quickly.

notes:
FORMATION:
{物|もの} (things) + {覚|おぼ}え (remembering)
→ The ability to remember things

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{物覚|ものおぼ}えがいい/いい - to have a good memory
・{物覚|ものおぼ}えが{悪|わる}い - to have a bad memory
・{物覚|ものおぼ}えが{早|はや}い - to be a quick learner
・{物覚|ものおぼ}えが{遅|おそ}い - to be a slow learner

USAGE:
Refers specifically to the practical ability to memorize and learn things, rather than memories themselves ({思|おも}い{出|で}) or the mental faculty of memory ({記憶|きおく}).

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{記憶力|きおくりょく} - Memory capacity/power (more formal)
・{暗記力|あんきりょく} - Memorization ability
